parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This is a presentation-layer controller, so the rubric fails it if it holds a business rule: a domain invariant, calculation or decision that the domain or application layer should own. Most of the controller is fine. Its constructor injects ReceivingService and CycleCountService from the business layer, which presentation may depend on. pick() just hands off to the service. count() turns the service result into a response shape ({ ok: d === null, delta }), which is normal presentation work.

The problem is receive(). It checks that a received quantity is a positive whole number (`!Number.isInteger(dto.quantity) || dto.quantity <= 0`). That is a stock invariant, not a check on the request's format. It also throws the business layer's own error type, StockError, with a message that states the business rule. Because the rule sits in the controller, any other caller of ReceivingService.receive skips it. The domain layer should own and enforce it. Both candidate flags (logic-density and controller-business-logic on lines 12-18) match what the source shows.
